sentences.text: This ancient crocodylomorph reached an estimated length of approximately 1.1 meters.
The type species Isisfordia duncani was discovered in the Winton Formation in Isisford, Queensland, Australia, in the mid-1990s.
The initial discovery included most of the animal except for the front portion of the skull.
A later expedition found a complete skull that differed from the original specimen only in size.
In 2019, a second species named Isisfordia molnari was described based on a braincase found in the Griman Creek Formation near Lightning Ridge.
In 2020, Hart retained the species I. selaslophensis as distinct because the holotype did not overlap with specimen AM F125553.
Analysis showed Isisfordia possessed vertebrae with loose ball-and-socket joints and a secondary palate similar to modern crocodilians, allowing air to pass to the lungs without entering the mouth.
A 2021 study confirmed that Isisfordia is outside Eusuchia and is the sister taxon to Paralligatoridae.
Isisfordia lived in Australia during the Middle Cretaceous, specifically the Albian to Cenomanian stages.
This corresponds to a time between 106.3 and 93.9 million years ago.
